culture.hint: Tap anything from Tunisia or Venezuela to discover it
culture.harissa.title: Harissa
culture.harissa.text: Tunisia’s red chili paste: sun-dried peppers pounded with garlic, caraway and coriander, finished with olive oil. In 2022 UNESCO added harissa to its list of intangible cultural heritage.
culture.door.title: The blue door
culture.door.text: Tunisian doors are painted bright blue or yellow and studded with black nail heads in patterns. The brass hand knocker, the khamsa, is said to keep bad luck away.
culture.jasmine.title: Jasmine
culture.jasmine.text: Jasmine is Tunisia’s flower. In summer, small jasmine bouquets called mechmoum are sold in the streets, and wearing one tucked behind the ear is a classic. Look at the toad.
culture.cage.title: Sidi Bou Said birdcage
culture.cage.text: Sidi Bou Said, a white-and-blue village on a cliff above the sea near Tunis, is famous for its blue doors and its domed white-and-blue birdcages.
culture.palm.title: Date palm
culture.palm.text: Tunisia’s southern oases, like Tozeur, grow Deglet Nour, the “dates of light”, named for their translucent amber colour.
culture.carthage.title: Carthage
culture.carthage.text: Once one of the great cities of the ancient Mediterranean, Carthage is now a seaside suburb of Tunis. Its ruins are a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
culture.camel.title: A camel from Douz
culture.camel.text: Douz, on the edge of the Sahara, is called the gateway to the desert. Every winter it hosts the International Festival of the Sahara, with camel races.
culture.couscous.title: Kosksi
culture.couscous.text: Couscous is the big family meal in many Tunisian homes. In 2020 UNESCO listed couscous traditions, a joint nomination by Tunisia, Algeria, Mauritania and Morocco.
culture.mosaic.title: Bardo mosaics
culture.mosaic.text: The Bardo Museum in Tunis holds one of the world’s largest collections of Roman mosaics, many found at sites like Carthage and El Jem.
culture.araguaney.title: Araguaney
culture.araguaney.text: Venezuela’s national tree. In the dry season it drops its leaves and the whole crown turns gold.
culture.turpial.title: Turpial
culture.turpial.text: Venezuela’s national bird: bright orange, black and white, with a loud whistled song.
culture.hammock.title: Chinchorro
culture.hammock.text: A chinchorro is a hand-woven hammock. On hot Venezuelan afternoons, a nap in one is serious business.
culture.cuatro.title: Cuatro
culture.cuatro.text: A small guitar with four strings. It keeps the rhythm of joropo, Venezuela’s national music and dance.
culture.arepas.title: Arepas
culture.arepas.text: Round corn-flour breads cooked on a flat griddle called a budare, then split and filled: cheese, black beans, or reina pepiada, a chicken and avocado salad.
culture.angel.title: Salto Ángel
culture.angel.text: Angel Falls, in Canaima National Park, is the highest uninterrupted waterfall in the world, about 979 m, pouring off Auyán-tepui, a flat-topped mountain.
culture.chiguire.title: Chigüire
culture.chiguire.text: The capybara, the world’s largest rodent, is called chigüire in Venezuela and lives in the rivers and wetlands of the Llanos. This one found a mandarin.
culture.catatumbo.title: Catatumbo lightning
culture.catatumbo.text: Over Lake Maracaibo, where the Catatumbo River flows in, silent lightning flickers on as many as 260 nights a year. Sailors once used it as a lighthouse.
culture.orchid.title: One pot, both of you
culture.orchid.text: These orchids grow in blue-and-white pottery like the kind made in Nabeul, Tunisia. And the orchid is Venezuela’s national flower, the Flor de Mayo.
culture.orchid.meaning: my love, in Spanish and in Arabic
